headings.title: Server startup, login and durable shutdown

html:
Server startup, login and durable shutdown

The Server makes its login and lifecycle pages available before controller restoration finishes. A single bootstrap owner constructs the controller, enters its lifespan, publishes readiness and later waits for durable shutdown. The browser observes that lifecycle; refreshing or closing a page does not restart restoration or release the controller's state owner.

Operator commands and recovery steps belong to Install and startup. This page explains the checked-out implementation and its ownership boundaries.

Console data and lifecycle flows trace the independent diagnostic sidecar, its cached observations, local GPU readings and explicit stack capture. Diagnostic findings do not establish task completion.

Owners and entry points

Owner Responsibility
Distribution context Recognizes source, legacy native images and compiled module builds; constructs matching resource paths and worker commands. Environment variables cannot activate packaged identity.
Packaged entrypoint Parses role-specific launch options, applies packaged defaults, configures Server login and delegates to the existing Server/Gateway startup owner.
Web bundle Supervises API, Manual and Console listeners with shared TLS selection, bind settings and a generation-bound restart token.
Uvicorn adapter Applies Server bind settings, formats early errors and returns the distinct SSL-context failure status understood by the bundle.
HTTPS protocol adapter On TLS-configured launches through the Uvicorn adapter, separates TLS traffic from plaintext HTTP and redirects plaintext on the same port.
Startup Server Serves the outer ASGI shell and owns the single inner controller lifespan.
Portal authentication Applies the installation's owner login, origin/CSRF checks and session lifecycle before controller routes.
Lifecycle reports Retains bounded observations in RAM and optional private timing history.
Lifecycle pages Renders detached startup/shutdown snapshots using shared packaged assets.

Source startup and packaged Server launch converge on the web bundle. A direct Uvicorn launch can use smto_runtime.server:create_app without that supervisor; it does not automatically acquire the bundle's sidecar/restart behavior. Embedded callers can still use the eager controller factory. A packaged Gateway selects its own inbound or outbound transport and is not a child of the Server web bundle.

TLS and plaintext requests

When smto_runtime.serve receives certificate/key options or their Uvicorn environment defaults, it selects https_redirect.RedirectConfig. The listener selects the protocol from the first received bytes and replays those bytes into the TLS protocol's buffer, preserving a fragmented ClientHello. TLS traffic reaches the configured application; plaintext HTTP reaches a separate redirect application, which returns 307 with the validated Host authority and the original raw path/query. It ignores forwarded-host/protocol headers and returns 400 for an invalid authority or target. No second listener port is opened. Negotiation is bounded to ten seconds, and idle negotiating sockets participate in graceful shutdown. API, Manual and Console listeners share this behavior. With no TLS context, ordinary HTTP behavior remains. A direct launch using the upstream uvicorn CLI bypasses this adapter.

From listening to ready

stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Initializing: outer ASGI lifespan starts Initializing --> Ready: inner lifespan entered successfully Initializing --> Failed: construction or startup fails Initializing --> Stopping: cooperative stop requested Ready --> Stopping: lifespan exits Stopping --> Closed: restoration and finalization finish Failed --> Stopping: outer service exits Closed --> [*]

StartupServer preloads its small asset allowlist and installs portal authentication before its lifespan launches the bootstrap task. Construction runs in a worker thread. Context-local observation follows that thread, so nested restore/reconciliation work can publish progress without exposing stores to the HTTP status handlers.

Only after the inner application's lifespan enters successfully does the shell publish _runtime and mark itself ready. Until then, recognized browser pages render lifecycle progress; other runtime HTTP requests receive 503. Unsupported early WebSockets close with 1013, or receive an HTTP 503 when the ASGI server supports that extension. Initialization responses include Retry-After: 1.

/livez measures the listening web service. /healthz depends on runtime readiness. /api/startup exposes the detailed current lifecycle report to a signed-in owner; ?view=summary returns a small status/lifecycle/instance projection. Anonymous health probes retain HTTP availability status while removing detailed errors and instance data. A separately authenticated installer update probe can obtain the limited build identity needed to verify a replacement.

Startup failure retains its innermost failed stage and structured error-catalog guidance. The shell stays available for diagnosis; a page refresh does not rerun the failed bootstrap. If shutdown arrives after construction but before lifespan entry, the bootstrap explicitly closes the constructed state owner. Cancelling an asyncio.to_thread waiter would not stop its worker, so the outer lifespan shields its bootstrap task until that owner actually finishes.

Login before controller state

AuthStore keeps versioned multi-account owner.json beneath the installation state root's .auth directory. This file is separate from controller databases, provider credentials and legal acceptance. The store checks ownership, private permissions and links, locks across processes, and replaces a flushed temporary file atomically. Windows validation uses the actual owner/DACL.

Passwords use a fresh salt and PBKDF2-SHA256 with the implementation's 600,000 iterations. Expensive verification has two process-wide slots; durable minute windows allow five attempts per client and account, with an aggregate budget of 200 counters. Successful login creates a fresh 12-hour session, stores its token hash and retains at most 128 sessions per account. Named local reset revokes that account's sessions. A verified password change keeps only the initiating session and its existing CSRF token; concurrent credential changes are detected before writing.

The ASGI boundary requires same-origin WebSockets and same-origin plus CSRF-token validation for unsafe browser HTTP methods. Cookies are HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, with Secure for HTTPS and separate names for HTTP recovery. Session revocation is checked during event streams and accepted WebSockets, which close when the session disappears. The outer shell marks its checked authentication directory so the inner app can avoid applying the same installation gate twice.

Gateway connection WebSockets, registered OAuth callbacks and narrowly enumerated artifact-token routes retain their own authentication contracts. Passing through those paths does not create owner scope. Missing or unsafe auth storage fails closed, while liveness and the fixed login assets remain available.

The installation graph owns configuration, model credentials and gateway registration. accounts.WorkspaceManager restores enabled accounts into independently owned Controller hubs and lifespans. Failed workspace recovery returns an unavailable workspace without blocking the authentication store, /user, or healthy accounts. Startup serializes shared bootstrap work; restored users retain their schedulers without an active browser login. Runtime work carries the actor, workspace ID and authorization revision. A shared admission queue enforces installation concurrency across accounts with round-robin queue selection. Activity admission also accounts for holders across user hives under one installation lock, retaining the existing total and gateway resource ceilings. Background HTTP and outbound gateway transports bind to their repository owner even without a request context.

Account APIs live under /api/admin/users. Each account has /password (POST), /sessions (DELETE), /gateways and /configuration (GET/PUT/PATCH) subresources. Account PATCH accepts identity, role, enabled state, gateway assignments and permitted configuration overrides. Scoped task policies cannot raise the current installation limits; global policy changes remain administrative operations.

Checkpoint manifest version 4 binds installation/workspace ownership and retains a separate storage-format version. Migration verifies a pre-upgrade copy before extracting shared authority, preserves configured legacy paths, and journals each phase. New account paths use immutable IDs. Workspace imports do not apply installation settings or alter the auth store. Disabled accounts cannot dispatch, and explicit re-enable does not resume paused work.

Gateway requests bind workspace ID and revision into authentication. Gateway jobs retain ownership through recovery fences. Durable revocation fences reject delayed requests; cleanup also tracks admitted requests and waits for confirmed termination. Deletion journals retain unresolved remote obligations, retire owned records/checkpoints only after drain, and preserve minimal actor/target audit records. OS process/file sandboxing is outside this application isolation boundary.

Application commands and restart

Human slash commands enter the command HTTP adapter, which constructs the registry, control plane and shared restart coordinator. The registry parses quoting, lowercases only the name, resolves exact aliases and invokes one handler. It does not create an AgentRequest, append a conversation turn or call a model. The UI tour owns the built-in command reference.

The Stop resolver maps /stop <number> to the open conversation's immutable task creation sequence. /stop all captures active native runs and preparation requests across conversations without the bounded UI-list limit. Both return explicit request/run contexts; the shared Stop dispatcher uses each task's summary preference and reports partial failures. Every target is revalidated at the existing native control endpoint, so a later continuation or navigation cannot redirect cancellation to a different task. Unstarted queued work and future schedules are outside this snapshot.

flowchart TD A[Human slash input and selected IDs] --> B[Validate HTTP shape and exact registry name] B --> C{Command scope} C -->|Conversation or run| D[Resolve current ownership and availability] D --> E[Return typed client action] E --> F[Client uses normal confirmation or control endpoint] F --> G[Revalidate command target before native mutation] C -->|Restart| H[Coalesce maintenance and enabled Gateway requests] H --> I[Send acknowledgement with prior instance identity] I --> J[Shared shielded Controller shutdown] J --> K{Final save confirmed?} K -->|Yes| L[Invoke restart callback or process handoff] K -->|No| M[Retain RAM and ownership for retry]

Context and result contracts constrain ID syntax, scope, presentation and client action vocabulary. They do not establish ownership. The control plane checks the selected conversation against tombstones, resolves request/run/task relationships and rejects superseded attempts for current controls. During preflight, a trace plus owned task/turn/current-run evidence lets stop work before a native checkpoint exists. Read-only trace can address an older owned attempt. At the native control endpoint, supplied command context is checked again under the task queue lock before mutation. Navigation actions do not inherit irrelevant run identities.

Status resolves only the selected conversation's lane or recorded last request. It never substitutes a global latest run. The projection allows known numeric context fields, a labeled measurement source, timing basis, queue count, persisted token rates and Memory diagnostics; unavailable measurements stay absent. Command diagnostic events include fixed registered identity, outcome/action category, timing and Gateway count, excluding raw arguments, private result text and handler exceptions. Unknown names and handler failures remain application errors.

Restart bypasses the task admission lock so active work cannot prevent acceptance. It still reserves maintenance ownership and uses the shared durable shutdown path. Enabled Gateways are normalized by transport/endpoint/node, deduplicated and requested with at most eight workers and a three-second timeout cap. Duplicate registry rows remain visible as skipped references, and the result retains registry order. Per-target failure does not abort the backend handoff. Unlike runtime purge, ordinary restart does not include disabled Gateways.

Gateway requests happen before the acknowledgement. Controller shutdown and handoff run in the server-only post-response callback; the public payload excludes that callable. Concurrent and duplicate callers share the same shielded restart task. Progress remains readable while shutdown waits, and caller disconnection does not cancel saving.

A failed final save leaves RAM and ownership available to the restart retry path. A failed process handoff after confirmed closure can retry without another save. Already accepted Gateway requests are not resent when retrying the Controller. The recovery action supplies /healthz, the previous instance ID and a 30-second client timeout; an initial restarting response is acknowledgement rather than proof of a new ready instance. Source, packaged and compiled-shared launch modes construct their respective process/module arguments through the existing runtime supervisor helpers.

The historical /api/agent/restart endpoint uses this same coordinator while retaining its legacy singular Gateway fields. During a reported shutdown, the command execution route rejects other submissions with HTTP 503 and admits only the trimmed, case-insensitive /restart, /shutdown and /shutdownserver spellings.

/shutdown and /shutdownserver use the same coordinator, so a restart and a shutdown can never both own the process: while one is accepted and not failed, any later lifecycle request returns that result. /shutdown sends /shutdown to every enabled, deduplicated Gateway; /shutdownserver sends none. A Gateway runs restart's admission fence, managed-LLM refusal and owned-execution drain, acknowledges stopping, then closes its service owners and exits with status 0 while the fence stays up. Gateways without the endpoint report unsupported, and the embedded LocalMachine Gateway reports that it follows the server lifecycle. The Controller then performs the shared final save with failure retention, marks the shutdown report stopped, and exits with status 0 (the web-bundle supervisor stops Manual and Console through a generation-bound shutdown.request token). Status 0 keeps Restart=on-failure and launchd SuccessfulExit=false services stopped. The report carries shutdown_requested, which lets the lifecycle page show Server stopped after the listener disappears and offer Retry shutdown after a failed save. The result uses the shutdown presentation and an await_backend_shutdown client action.

Measurements and durable shutdown

startup.py publishes static phase labels and numeric counters while iterating existing work. It does not make a second data pass to count progress. The report retains at most 2,048 phases and 32 samples per unit; counters must be finite, nonnegative and nondecreasing. Ordinary counter events are throttled to a quarter second. Snapshot reads copy RAM without SQL, filesystem probes or controller repository locks.

Live estimates need at least three samples spanning two seconds, with a recent last sample. Otherwise compatible historical timings can provide an estimate; unknown or waiting work stays unknown. Parent estimates cover their children and are not counted twice. Source records, constructed entities and processed bytes are distinct counters, not interchangeable percentages.

Optional startup-history.json and shutdown-history.json retain up to 30 runs, including at most five matching schema/source runs used for estimation. History is bounded to two MiB and written through private temporary files. It is timing evidence for this installation, not a recovery checkpoint or readiness decision. /diagnostics/startup renders the current process's retained startup report.

ShutdownReport records the lifecycle owner's stop, drain, final-save and release phases. Only the owner confirms a durable generation. Deferred removal of obsolete files is tracked separately and cannot undo an already confirmed save. The controller's state and recovery contract owns the actual persistence decision.

The shared Controller shutdown owner marks work as stopping before service teardown can block. Registered cleanups run in reverse order, followed by tracked-work drain and the hub's final close. Most service-stop errors are logged and teardown continues; an owner explicitly marked to retain state on cleanup failure aborts that handoff. Concurrent restart/lifespan requests share the same attempt. Caller cancellation is held until the shielded save task finishes, then propagated.

A failed restart can retry saving without repeating completed service stops. Optional shutdown timing-history failure does not undo a confirmed save. The terminal reporter joins its heartbeat before printing the final result and distinguishes an unconfirmed save from durable success with cleanup still pending. Existing terminal messages say “SQL save”; that wording covers the current mixed recovery generation, including native binary snapshots, and does not imply live requests use SQL. The reporter observes the owner's result and cannot independently release ownership or declare data saved.

The web supervisor sends one termination signal to live children. Auxiliary listeners share a 15-second cleanup deadline; the API child has no supervisor kill deadline because its lifespan may still be saving. A successful restart request is written with the current bundle token only after durable controller shutdown. The supervisor then replaces its listeners. A dedicated SSL-context failure can request an HTTP retry; arbitrary application failures do not request that fallback.

The TLS listener contract also applies after a successful bundle restart. During the certificate-failure fallback, listeners serve ordinary HTTP without a TLS redirect.

Compiled replacement

Server update contracts reuse the Gateway package/journal primitives, with a distinct state format and explicit Server variant. Compatibility requires the target, compiled backend, feature variant and updater/controller protocols to match. A descriptor binds the exact URL, size, checksum, build and legal versions; its validation does not itself authorize or execute installation.

Controller admission and final-save handoff

The Server update coordinator connects three distinct owners: controller RAM holds execution admission, the installation-private journal holds local update authority, and an independent installer owns replacement. Restoring workspace data on another installation cannot authorize an update: reconciliation marks active database operations failed unless they match that installation's private journal.

The Settings routes expose public status, source configuration, metadata preview, acceptance, cancellation and final-save retry. Portal middleware supplies authentication and CSRF protection. Status responses disable caching, and operation responses omit private installation records and readiness tokens. A custom preview is valid for one hour and binds the exact descriptor, current build and instance. Accepting the same active selection returns its operation; a different selection conflicts. Changing the discovery source does not change an already accepted package.

Boundary Evidence required before advancing
Accept selection Supported installed instance, compatible descriptor, current registry identity and no conflicting maintenance/update operation
Stop admitted work Cancellation is recorded and owned process exit is verified; new execution remains held
Start independent helper The requested controller checkpoint epoch/revision has been durably saved
Begin final shutdown A matching independent helper has acknowledged ownership and prepared a candidate
Permit replacement Durable close succeeded and the journal contains drained with this operation's saved_operation_id
Release new execution The helper accepted the returning installation's readiness proof and settled activation
flowchart LR A[Owner selects exact package] --> B[RAM admission and local journal] B --> C[Cancel work and verify process exit] C --> D[Checkpoint confirmed] D --> E[Independent helper prepares] E --> F[Controller final save] F --> G[Matching durable save receipt] G --> H[Replacement and readiness verification]

Admission helpers inspect the active operation within existing task/native transactions. waiting_for_tasks now means stopping work, including captured tasks, paused runs, requests and continuation descendants. New execution is fenced immediately in every active account workspace. Never-started tasks stay queued. Monitors, comparisons, inference operations/jobs, downloads and exports are cancelled; managed models retain restart intent.

Cancellation owners share two seconds for cleanup, then terminate surviving owned process trees and verify exit for up to five seconds. Remote cancellation attempts run concurrently with five-second deadlines; unresolved receipts survive restart for retry. A stopping failure retains the fence and exposes Retry update. Final save still requires successful durable close, even if stopping or saving needs a retry.

Maintenance reservations span the entire asynchronous request for TLS changes, imports, restart and runtime purge. Update acceptance also checks the installation lock, existing Gateway updates and pending maintenance state. Discovery has its own stop signal: final shutdown quiesces catalog writes while journal/helper supervision can continue after the RAM hub closes. The coordinator normally polls progress every half second and retries eligible helper recovery at five-second intervals.

A failed final save preserves the operation for retry. If writing the failure to the journal also fails, an in-memory status overlay keeps the retry control visible; it does not grant the helper a save receipt. Startup publishes build, variant, instance, process/supervisor and fresh-boot identity only after runtime initialization, including inference management readiness. Model recovery waits for activation to settle. rollback_failed keeps the execution fence in place for recovery.

See the Server update operator guide for selection, diagnostics, publication commands and native qualification limits. Coordination tests cover transactional admission, checkpoint/helper gates and retry after persistence errors; inference tests cover deferred model recovery and available stop controls.

Controller coordination of Gateway updates

GatewayUpdates owns the controller half of remote updates: metadata discovery, accepted target/package identity, whole-task draining, durable command dispatch and authenticated progress. It never downloads or installs the Gateway package. The Gateway owns its local work drain and the independent installer described below.

The shared release catalog supports both Server and Gateway descriptor contracts. It reads bounded metadata with ETags, skips draft/prerelease/unpublished releases and waits for uploaded package/descriptor pairs with matching release identity, size and advertised digest. Invalid or incomplete enumeration retains the last trusted release set and records an error. Offers require the installed build to appear in the selected target/variant catalog; publication time and release ID determine order. Unknown versions are not guessed from their labels. Custom previews bind selected URLs to validated bytes and compatibility facts without fetching the package.

Each Gateway operation captures URL, node, peer key, enrollment generation, installed build and the boot identity observed at acceptance. Preview acceptance rechecks the target identity, installed build, compatibility and its one-hour lifetime. Capability observations are probed roughly every minute and become unusable for acceptance after two minutes; restored observations start stale. Catalog availability can still be shown while connection verification is pending.

The admission helpers evaluate the global Server fence and every accepted Gateway target in the same RAM transaction as task/native admission. Acceptance captures the tasks and runs to cancel, including multi-Gateway work and tasks between attempts. Continuations are fenced immediately. Never-started work stays queued. Cancellation intent and resulting history are checkpointed before the Gateway install command is sent. Lost acknowledgements reuse the same operation ID. Gateways advertising updater.stops_work stop their own local workloads; published older builds use their existing authenticated cancellation APIs. Unsupported workloads produce explicit compatibility failures and retry controls.

Observation or action Controller responsibility
Direct management Use the configured Gateway client's authenticated connection and bounded JSON replies
Outbound management Require the connected session's Gateway ID and verified peer identity to match
Cancellation during stopping Disabled; cancellation cannot restore interrupted work
Cancellation during package preparation Require the unchanged target's authenticated cancelled response
verifying_connection Probe the expected new build, readiness and a fresh boot before confirming
completed Recheck the running new build/readiness/fresh boot before releasing the hold
rolled_back Verify that the previous build is running and ready
Lost contact Preserve the last installation phase and record connectivity uncertainty separately

After five minutes of pending reconnection, the public projection adds delayed connection guidance. Network loss alone neither confirms success nor requests rollback. A reported rollback_failed remains fenced and outside the supervisor's automatic retry loop. Terminal receipts cannot be overwritten by late progress patches. The normal worker advances active operations at two-second intervals or on a wake signal; catalog discovery runs independently.

The Gateway operator guide owns package, publication and recovery instructions. Coordination tests exercise acceptance races and readiness evidence; source tests cover immutable previews and isolated HTTPS metadata; persistence tests cover checkpoint restoration; transport tests cover signed commands and cancellation with installation effects isolated.

Independent replacement and readiness

Helper launch creates an owner outside the application's process/service lifetime and requires a matching process acknowledgement before activation. The helper holds its own lease and journals every phase. Shared staging checks free space, HTTPS redirects, declared size/checksum, safe archive extraction and the launcher's exact --version identity before preparing a candidate.

The Server helper waits for drained and saved_operation_id matching its operation before replacement. A save failure can remain pending for retry without a helper-imposed kill timer. The replacement must report a new boot, matching build/variant/instance, controller and supervisor identities, and local API readiness. Enabled Manual/Console listeners must belong to the new bundle as well. Only then is the operation completed.

Gateway activation instead waits for its live checkpoint/drain acknowledgement, verifies the new local process and moves to verifying_connection; the controller owns reconnection confirmation. A failed or interrupted activation attempts to restore the previous installation. rolled_back records verified recovery; rollback_failed preserves the unresolved outcome for intervention. Those states are not interchangeable with successful installation.

The early update HTTP adapter keeps owner-visible durable status available through startup and shutdown. Without a live update owner it reads the journal but disallows changes. Operator controls and cancellation rules are documented under Server updates.

Regression evidence

Startup-server fixtures exercise responsive progress, readiness gates, shutdown during restoration and real state restoration. Report fixtures cover estimate thresholds, history compatibility and snapshot reads without I/O. Shutdown-screen fixtures cover the final-save fence and retry observations. Portal-auth fixtures cover private storage, CSRF, sessions, password changes and independently authenticated routes. Bundle TLS fixtures use isolated listeners to check restart/protocol selection without model workloads. Server update fixtures cover the final-save gate, stale readiness and rollback; Gateway update fixtures cover descriptor integrity, interrupted downloads and independent helper ownership. These are test entrypoints; execution results and any unresolved failures are recorded in the refresh status.
